instrument_name: GA DOR Employer's Withholding Tax Guide 2026 (rev. September 2026), Percentage Method Tables E/F and worked examples
article_or_section: pp. 51-52 (Tables E, F; Examples 1 and 2); p. 31 ff. Tax Tables A-D
figure_or_rule_carried: Percentage method: (1) wages less standard deduction per period [annual 30,000 MFJ / 15,000 Single-HoH / 15,000 MFS; weekly 576.92/288.46/288.46; biweekly 1,153.85/576.92; semimonthly 1,250.00/625.00; monthly 2,500.00/1,250.00; quarterly 7,500/3,750; semiannual 15,000/7,500; daily 82.19/41.10]; (2) less dependent allowance per dependent [annual 5,000; weekly 96.15; biweekly 192.31; semimonthly 208.33; monthly 416.67; quarterly 1,250; semiannual 2,500; daily 13.70]; (3) x 4.99%. Married couples both earning use MFS column. Example 1 (MFJ semimonthly 2,000, 1 dependent): 2,000-1,250-208.33=541.67 x 0.0499 = 27.03 (re-derived 27.029333). Example 2 (HoH biweekly 935, 2 dependents): 0.00. Tax tables (pp. 31-50) priced at the upper bound of each wage bracket: Single weekly 276-294 -> 0.28 = (294-288.46) x 0.0499 = 0.2764 (re-derived). Guide states tables and percentage method give slightly different results; no rounding instruction (cents).

instrument_name: GA DOR Employer's Withholding Tax Guide 2026: Withholding due dates and Withholding Requirements Summary
figure_or_rule_carried: Payer status by lookback (12 months ending 30 June prior year): semi-weekly if > 50,000 (EFT; Wed/Thu/Fri payday -> following Wednesday; Sat-Tue -> following Friday; G-7 Schedule B quarterly); monthly if > 200/month (GA-V by 15th of following month; G-7 for monthly payer by last day of month after quarter); quarterly if <= 200/month and > 800/year (G-7 by last day of month after quarter); annual if <= 800/year (G-7 by 31 January, request via GTC). One-day rule: > 100,000 withheld for a payday -> EFT next banking day. Any G-7 > 500 -> EFT thereafter and mandatory e-filing; EFT failure penalty 10%. Zero G-7 required while account active. 2026 dates: Q3 G-7 2026-11-02; Q4 G-7 2027-02-01. Registration on GTC (gtc.dor.ga.gov), number and frequency issued within 15 minutes. Final G-7 within 30 days of ceasing to have employees. Late payment penalty 25 + 5%/month, cap 25 + 25%; interest prime + 3%.

instrument_name: GA DOR Employer's Withholding Tax Guide 2026: Income Statement Reporting Requirements (G-1003, W-2, 1099)
figure_or_rule_carried: W-2s and 1099-NEC with GA withholding filed with Form G-1003 by 31 January (TY2026: 2027-02-01); other 1099s by 28 February (2027-03-01); W-2 not required if no GA withholding. Electronic filing mandatory if federally required to e-file, or if paying by EFT (mandatory or voluntary). Formats: GTC manual entry, G-1003 template/CSV, or Federal Format (EFW2) with Georgia-defined RS record (TY2026 specs 'available late October 2026'); 1099 via IRIS XML (FIRE/Pub 1220 no longer accepted from TY2026). GA does not participate in CF/SF for statements with GA withholding. TY2026: qualified overtime (W-2 box 12 TT) and cash tips (box 12 TP, box 14b TTOC) reported on W-2; RLA employees 'GA OT' in box 14a; no separate G-7 fields in 2026; from 2027 G-7 collects quarterly overtime/tip totals and employee counts. Business closing: statements due 30 days after final wages. Late statement penalties 10/20/50 per statement (caps 50k/100k/200k).

instrument_name: GA DOR Employer's Withholding Tax Guide 2026: definitions, G-4, special payments
figure_or_rule_carried: Resident: legal resident, or lives in GA on regular/permanent basis, or 183+ days in 365-day period ending 31 Dec. Taxable nonresident: > 5% of wages or > 5,000 attributable to GA. Residents working in another state: no GA withholding if the other state requires withholding. G-4 (name, address, SSN, filing status, allowances, additional withholding); no G-4 -> use W-4 if sufficient, else Single zero allowances; G-4 claiming exempt or > 14 allowances mailed to DOR; exempt G-4 valid until 15 February following year; new G-4 effective first payroll after receipt. Bonuses: rate in effect when paid (5.19% before 2026-05-11, may use 4.99% from 2026-05-11). Domestic workers (housekeepers, nannies), farm laborers and ministers: withholding not required (voluntary). Severance: withhold if resident when paid; nonresident at payment -> no GA withholding. 401(k)/profit-sharing/deferred comp: GA follows federal, pre-tax. 1099-NEC without valid TIN: 6% for labor in GA. Payroll records retained >= 4 years.

instrument_name: GDOL Employer Handbook DOL-224 (R-11/24): Quarterly Tax and Wage Reports (DOL-4N), domestic annual DOL-4, multiple worksite report, records
figure_or_rule_carried: DOL-4N Quarterly Tax and Wage Report due last day of month after quarter (30 Apr, 31 Jul, 31 Oct, 31 Jan); employers with 25+ employees must file and pay electronically; channels: Employer Portal direct entry (<=100 employees), Internet Wage File Upload CSV/Excel (100-15,000), SFTP (>15,000 and payroll service providers); paper DOL-4N allowed below 25 employees. Wages reported in the quarter actually paid. Domestic-only employers: annual DOL-4 by 31 January with quarterly wages (34-8-150). Multiple Worksite Report quarterly (statistical supplement). Corrections on DOL-3C. Records (34-8-121): full name and full SSN, hire/rehire dates, separation date and reason, quarterly wages incl. cash value of other remuneration and tips; retain >= 7 years. Rate notices DOL-626 posted to Employer Portal by 31 December (no longer mailed).

instrument_name: GDOL Employer Handbook DOL-224 (R-11/24): UI coverage, wages defined, non-covered employment, rate computation
figure_or_rule_carried: Liability: private employer with 1+ worker in 20 weeks or 1,500 payroll in a quarter; agricultural 10+ workers in 20 weeks or 20,000 cash in a quarter; domestic 1,000 cash in a quarter; 501(c)(3) 4+ workers in 20 weeks; government reports quarterly (mostly reimbursing). Corporate officers are employees. Wages include bonuses, board and lodging (minimum value by GDOL rule), vacation pay, tips (to FUTA extent), employee 401(k) deferrals; not wages: employer 401(k), Section 125 premiums (employer and employee), WC payments, accounted business expenses. Non-covered: sole proprietor's parent/spouse/children under 21, elected officials, casual labor < 50, student nurses, newspaper carriers < 18, commission-only insurance and real-estate agents, students in work-study programs, church/religious-order employees, inmates, certain direct sellers. New employer 2.7% until 36 months chargeable; experienced rate from reserve ratio (taxes - charges)/3-yr average payroll at 30 June computation date, statutory tables; voluntary contributions within 30 days of notice. Common paymaster allowed. SUTA dumping penalty: highest rate + >= 2 points, 4 years.

instrument_name: GDOL Employer Handbook DOL-224 (R-11/24): Separation Notice DOL-800 (O.C.G.A. 34-8-190(c), GDOL Rule 300-2-7-.06) and Mass Separation Notice DOL-402
figure_or_rule_carried: DOL-800 Separation Notice (form R-02-24) required for every separated worker regardless of reason, stating the reason; delivered on the last day of work, or mailed to the last known address within 3 days of the separation occurring or becoming known. Mass Separation Notice DOL-402 + DOL-402A to GDOL within 48 hours when 25+ workers separated same day for the same reason (lack of work) for 7+ days, or in a labor dispute. Vacation pay: no state law, matter of agreement (FLSA silent). Sales representative commissions paid within 30 days after termination of the representation agreement (non-waivable).

instrument_name: GDOL Employer Handbook DOL-224 (R-11/24): Wage and hour requirements (minimum wage, overtime, frequency, methods, deductions, garnishment, new hire, child labor)
figure_or_rule_carried: Most employers follow federal minimum wage 7.25/h; Georgia minimum wage 5.15/h applies only in rare cases not covered by FLSA. Overtime: FLSA rules (over 40/workweek at 1.5x); no state daily overtime. Frequency: semi-monthly or more frequent, except officers/superintendents/heads paid monthly. Methods: money, check, or credit transfer (direct deposit) with consent; payroll cards; full net amount; at least one free access. Deductions: no Georgia law listing permitted voluntary deductions or requiring written consent (written authorization recommended); no law against requiring purchase of uniforms/tools (FLSA floor applies). Garnishment: generally one attachment at a time, but child support order and tax levy may run simultaneously. New hire: O.C.G.A. 19-11-9.2 and 42 USC 653a, report new hires and rehires within 10 days of hire to the Georgia New Hire Reporting Program (ga-newhire.com), incl. one-day workers and returns after layoff/leave. Child labor: Employment Certificate DOL-4103 (work permit) kept on the work site for all workers under 18; minors in entertainment DOL-4101; under-16 barred from mills, factories, laundries etc.; most-protective of state/federal applies.

instrument_name: Georgia HB 463 (2026), 'Georgia Economic Growth and Tax Relief Act of 2026', as passed House and Senate (HB 463/AP)
figure_or_rule_carried: Rate 4.99% for taxable years beginning on/after 2026-01-01 (was 5.19%); reduced by 0.125 point annually from 2027-01-01 until 3.99%, each step delayed one year if any OPB trigger (revenue estimate < +3%, net revenue not above each of prior 3 years, Revenue Shortfall Reserve insufficient) holds at 1 December; OPB reports by 1 December. Standard deduction 30,000 MFJ / 15,000 single-HoH-MFS, +750 / +375 annually from 2027 to 36,000 / 18,000 (same delay triggers). Dependent exemption 5,000, +125 annually from 2027 to 6,000. Qualified overtime (IRC s.225) up to 1,750 for full-time hourly employees 2026-2028 (repealed 2028-12-31); cash tips up to 1,750 from 2026; employers report totals and employee counts monthly/quarterly with withholding returns (2026 may be annual). Act effective on Governor's approval, applicable to taxable years beginning on/after 2026-01-01. ENACTMENT: in force - signed by the Governor 2026-05-11 (GA DOR guide 2026, US-GA-001/US-GAS5-004) and the identical file (md5 match) is published by the Office of the Governor under '2026 signed legislation' (https://gov.georgia.gov/document/2026-signed-legislation/hb-463/download, read 2026-11-02); Act number not read. OPERATING LEVEL: rate and deductions operate at assessment (annual return) and are mirrored in withholding by DOR tables from 2026-05-11; the OT/tip subtractions operate at assessment only (DOR: do not reduce withholding).

instrument_name: Georgia Form G-4 Employee's Withholding Allowance Certificate (Rev. 06/03/26)
figure_or_rule_carried: Fields: 1a name, 1b SSN, 2a/2b address; 3 marital status letter A Single / B MFS or MFJ both working / C MFJ one working / D Head of Household (letter selects the employer tax table); 4 dependent allowances; 5 Georgia adjustments allowances (worksheet: (itemized - standard deduction 15,000 single-HoH-MFS / 30,000 MFJ) + GA adjustments - non-wage income, / 5,000, remainder > 2,500 rounds up); 6 additional withholding per period; 7 letter and total allowances (4+5); 8a exempt (no GA liability last year and none expected; Form 500 line 16 = 0); 8b Military Spouses Residency Relief / SCRA exempt (states of residence); 9 employer name, address, FEIN, WH#. Employer mails form only if > 14 allowances or exempt. Do not accept additional allowances without worksheet, or exempt with numbers on lines 4-7. MSRRA spouse: employer reports none of the wages as Georgia wages on W-2.

instrument_name: GA DOR Federal Format Layout page and Federal_Format_Specs.pdf (RS record for W-2 with G-1003)
figure_or_rule_carried: Georgia accepts EFW2 with a GA-defined RS record: positions 1-2 'RS', 3-4 state code (EFW2), SSN 10-18 (zeros if none), employee name/address per EFW2, SQUI fields blank, 248-267 state employer account number, 274-275 state code, 276-286 state taxable wages, 287-297 state income tax withheld, 298-307 period end date MM/DD/YYYY, 308 tax type code, local fields blank, 331-339 withholding number (no hyphen, upper-case alpha, 9 chars), employer name and addresses. The file posted at the URL on 2026-11-02 is Rev 01/18; the TY2026 layout with the 'GA OT' (RLA overtime, W-2 box 14a) field that the 2026 guide announces for 'late October 2026' was NOT on the page at retrieval. Use Rev 01/18 only as the structural base.

instrument_name: Georgia State Directory of New Hires (Georgia DHS): FAQ and Compliance pages (O.C.G.A. 19-11-9.2; 42 U.S.C. 653a)
authority: Georgia Department of Human Services, Georgia State Directory of New Hires
article_or_section: FAQ 'Basics of New Hire Reporting'; Compliance page
figure_or_rule_carried: All GA employers (public and private) report new hires, rehires and returning workers within 10 days of hire date (electronic filers: two monthly transmissions not more than 16 days apart). Data: employer FEIN (same FEIN as quarterly wage reports), name, full address; employee name (first, middle, last), full address, SSN, date of birth, start date, medical insurance availability, state of hire. Channels: online entry/file upload on the site, FTP, fax or mail (P.O. Box 92364, Atlanta, GA 30314-4123). Report employees who reside or work in GA, even one-day workers. Penalty (federal option): up to 25 per unreported hire, 500 if conspiracy. www.ga-newhire.com redirects to newhire-reporting.com/GA-Newhire (DHS copyright).

instrument_name: Georgia SB 160 (2023), Act 86, as passed: O.C.G.A. 34-8-151 new-employer contribution rate schedule and 34-8-155 sunset dates
figure_or_rule_carried: New/newly covered employer contribution 2.64% for 2017-01-01..2026-12-31 (34-8-151(d)) plus 0.06% administrative assessment 2024-2026 (34-8-181) = 2.70% total in 2026; from 2027-01-01 contribution 2.7% (34-8-151(a): 'after December 31, 2026') and Article 6 assessment repealed (34-8-185), so total new-employer rate 2027 = 2.70% with no assessment, absent new legislation. Experience variations: 34-8-155(e) table applies through 2026-12-31, 34-8-155(c) table from 2027-01-01 (table contents not in the act text read). Assessment is employer-only, reported on the quarterly tax and wage report, never deducted from wages.

instrument_name: SB 255 (2015-2016), House Judiciary Committee substitute LC 29 7118S: new O.C.G.A. Title 18 Chapter 4 (garnishment)
figure_or_rule_carried: Ordinary garnishment of earnings per workweek: lesser of 25% of disposable earnings or the amount by which weekly disposable earnings exceed 217.00 (text reads '$217.00'; for other periods a multiple of 7.25/h) - the federal CCPA floor 30 x 7.25 = 217.50 is the binding federal minimum (15 U.S.C. 1673, US-FED-011), so the build applies the more protective figure; limit applies across multiple ordinary garnishments unless a continuing garnishment for support is served. No discharge for garnishment for any one obligation. Continuing garnishment for support: max 50% of weekly disposable earnings (18-4-53(b)); first applied to current periodic support accrued daily (annual / 365), excess to original arrearage (18-4-54). Garnishee may deduct the greater of 50.00 or 10% of the amount paid into court, not to exceed 100.00, as expenses (18-4-14). Retirement funds exempt until distributed. ENACTMENT: this is the committee substitute text; the enacted act number and later amendments (2020 SB 443, 2021 changes named in tier-B leads) were NOT read on an official host, so figures are 'as of the 2016 substitute'.

instrument_name: SB 201 (2017-2018), House Industry and Labor Committee substitute LC 36 3365S: O.C.G.A. 34-1-10 (Family Care Act, use of sick leave for immediate family)
figure_or_rule_carried: Employers with 25+ employees (incl. State and political subdivisions) that provide sick leave must let employees working 30+ hours/week use up to 5 days of earned sick leave per calendar year to care for a child, spouse, grandchild, grandparent, parent or tax dependent; no duty to offer sick leave; excludes employers offering an ESOP; no new cause of action. Georgia has no paid sick leave mandate (GDOL FAQ, US-GAS5-016). ENACTMENT: substitute text read; enacted version, original 2020 sunset and its later repeal/extension (tier-B lead: 2023) NOT confirmed on an official host; a 2021 bill (HB 197, 18 employees) was a proposal only. Effective date 2017-07-01 is from tier-B leads.

instrument_name: GDOL Individuals FAQs - Fair Labor Standards Act
figure_or_rule_carried: Overtime over 40 h/workweek at 1.5x (FLSA), no state daily overtime, no weekend/night premium; tipped employees: 2.13/h cash wage if tips bring pay to the federal minimum; no severance-pay requirement; neither FLSA nor Georgia law requires breaks or meal periods; neither federal nor state law requires vacation, sick or personal leave; employment at will. (Full re-read of the page cited by US-GA-P5-1-004.)

instrument_name: HB 1157 (2025-2026 session, LC 52 0657, as introduced): bill to repeal O.C.G.A. 34-4-3.1 - quotes the current text of 34-4-3.1 (local wage/benefit/scheduling preemption)
figure_or_rule_carried: Current law quoted (34-4-3.1): every wage or employment-benefit mandate adopted by a local government entity (county, municipality, consolidated government, authority, board of education) is preempted; no local government may adopt or enforce one, nor use purchasing/contracting to influence vendor wages or benefits, nor regulate private-employer hours or scheduling. Consequence for payroll: no local minimum wage, local paid-leave or predictive-scheduling ordinance applies to private employers in Georgia (Atlanta etc. may set pay for their own employees only). STATUS of HB 1157: introduced bill, NOT enacted (no passage found; status page not read) - draft; the preemption stays in force.

instrument_name: O.C.G.A. 10-1-393.8 Protection from disclosure of SSN (Justia mirror, 2024 Code of Georgia) - lead only
figure_or_rule_carried: Lead (search summary only, page not read): prohibits publicly posting or displaying an individual's SSN, with exceptions for uses required by state or federal law. No Georgia rule located that requires SSN truncation on pay statements specifically. Needs an official-host read (enacting act on legis.ga.gov) before any stage cites it.

instrument_name: Georgia DHS Division of Child Support Services - For Employers (employer fees)
authority: Georgia Department of Human Services, Division of Child Support Services
article_or_section: Employer fees; Interest on Child Support Judgments (O.C.G.A. 19-11-7(e)); Payment Processing Fee
figure_or_rule_carried: Employer administrative fee for child-support income deduction: up to 25.00 to establish and up to 3.00 per deduction thereafter (DCSS: 108-216 per year). Payments go to the Georgia Family Support Registry. Payment processing fee charged to the non-custodial parent: lesser of 1.50 or 5% per payment (not an employer deduction). Interest 7% on DCSS judgments (arrears from 2007-01-01) - case-level, not payroll. Statutory cite for the employer fee is not given on the page.

instrument_name: GDOL Notice of Intended Action, 15 June 2026: proposed amendments to Rules 300-2-2, -3, -4, -5, -7 (Employment Security Law), with exact copies and synopsis
figure_or_rule_carried: Proposed (comments to 2026-07-16; adoption considered 2026-07-16): 300-2-2-.02 tax and wage reports carry full first/last name, valid SSN, quarterly wages; domestic-only employers annual by 31 January, others quarterly by last day of month after quarter; (6) ALL employers must file tax and wage reports electronically unless the department authorises otherwise (removes the 25-employee distinction - synopsis: 'eliminating distinctions based on employer size'); zero-wage quarters must still be reported; administrative assessment reported on the same report (11). 300-2-4-.10 Mass Separation Notice DOL-402/402A within 48 h when 25+ workers at one establishment separated same day for same reason (permanent, indefinite or 7+ days); a timely DOL-402 replaces individual DOL-800s. 300-2-7-.06 Separation Notice DOL-800 to every separated worker on the last day of work (electronic delivery allowed: email/self-service portal, retainable record, UETA e-signature), or within 3 days if unavailable, by email or mail; notice is for UI administration only. STATUS: proposed rule text; GDOL announced the updated rules on 2026-10-07 (US-GAS5-021) - adopted text and effective date not read. OPERATING LEVEL: employer reporting (UI).

instrument_name: GDOL news, 7 October 2026: 'Employers: Updated Rules Simplify Doing Business With GDOL'
figure_or_rule_carried: Rules updated (in force per the post, date not stated): quarterly wage reports may be filed on time with a placeholder SSN while a new hire's SSN is collected - format 000-00-0001, 000-00-0002 ... (sequential per missing-SSN record), electronic Employer Portal filing only; employer must document efforts and correct 'promptly' (GDOL: within 30 days after obtaining the valid SSN) on DOL-3C (mailed to Employer Accounts, Suite 752); Separation Notices may be delivered electronically or as signed hard copy, on the last day of work or within 3 days if unavailable; posters: physical at traditional worksites, electronic permitted for remote/hybrid workforces. The post does not mention the all-employer e-filing mandate proposed in 300-2-2-.02(6).

instrument_name: GDOL Minimum Wage page and Individuals FAQs - Laws and Regulations
article_or_section: Minimum Wage page; FAQ 'I quit my job and my employer refuses to pay me for my last week worked'
figure_or_rule_carried: Federal minimum wage 7.25/h (since 2009-07-24); Georgia minimum wage 5.15/h (O.C.G.A. 34-4-3), but with limited exceptions the federal rate applies. No 2027 increase enacted (none stated; local mandates preempted, US-GAS5-017). Final pay: GDOL answers the unpaid-last-week question only by reference to FLSA minimum wage/overtime and a Magistrate Court small-claims action - no Georgia final-pay timing statute is cited (absence consistent with the DOL-224 handbook, which has no final-pay rule, and 34-7-2, US-GAP9L-001). Georgia is a right-to-work state.

instrument_name: GA DOR 'Income Tax Federal Tax Changes' page (annual IRC conformity acts) read with O.C.G.A. 48-7-27(a) as quoted in HB 463 and the 2026 withholding guide
article_or_section: 2021-2024 entries; HB 463 Sec. 2-3 (48-7-27(a) starting point); guide pp. 4, 27
figure_or_rule_carried: Georgia taxable income starts from federal AGI (48-7-27(a), US-GAS5-009), and Georgia adopts the IRC annually by conformity act (HB 1162 for IRC as of 2024-01-01; per the 2026 guide HB 1199 conforms to the IRC as of 2026-01-01 with listed decouplings, US-GAS5-003). Payroll consequence: exclusions that keep wages out of federal AGI - 401(k)/403(b)/457 elective deferrals (guide: 'Georgia follows the federal guidelines', pre-tax), Section 125 premiums, HSA payroll contributions, qualified transportation fringes, group-term life up to 50,000 - are also out of Georgia wages (W-2 box 16 follows box 1); no Georgia departure for these located. Federal OBBBA-type overtime/tip deductions are NOT adopted as such: Georgia has its own limited 1,750 subtractions at assessment only (HB 463). The DOR conformity page itself was last updated for 2024 (no 2025/2026 entry at retrieval), so the HB 1199 detail rests on the guide.
